claims.text: The starting material is the HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
Adding 3–5 at.% W and applying a tailored heat treatment will produce fine tungsten-rich precipitates.
The proposed tungsten-rich precipitates will be coherent.
The proposed tungsten-rich precipitates will form both within grains and along grain boundaries.
The tungsten-rich precipitates will pin or obstruct dislocations.
The tungsten-rich precipitates will stabilize or pin grain boundaries.
Obstruction of dislocations and stabilization of grain boundaries will increase strain hardening.
The precipitate reinforcement will delay the initiation of shear bands during high-strain-rate deformation.
Delayed shear-band initiation will produce more uniform deformation and greater resistance to localization.
The intervention will increase yield strength by approximately 10–15% relative to the stated baseline.
The intervention will increase fracture strain from approximately 13.5% to 17–20%.
The intervention will enhance strain hardening under dynamic adiabatic loading.
The intervention will improve impact-induced energy absorption.
The predictions apply to adiabatic dynamic loading at strain rates from 10^3 to 10^4 s^-1.
The predicted improvements may not carry over directly to quasi-static or non-adiabatic loading.

contradictions.description: The intervention calls for a 'specific' or tailored heat treatment, but no temperature, duration, cooling rate, or other schedule is given, and the boundary field acknowledges that the heat-treatment parameters remain to be defined.

The quantified improvements under dynamic adiabatic loading are expressed relative to quasi-static baseline values. This is not a loading-condition-matched comparison, so the proposed percentage and fracture-strain changes conflate intervention effects with strain-rate effects.
